full_judgment:
6. Defendants pleaded that the suit property is their only homestead property and after death of their father they have inherited the same and, as such, there is no question of transfer of the homestead property by their father. They also pleaded that the suit is barred by limitation and that the allegation of selling the huts from the suit land by the father of the defendant to other persons is also concocted. 

 11. Here in this suit, the question of limitation is also very important because the plaintiff's case is that the agreement took place on 8th Ashin, 1389 BS and the money was paid on 10th Ashin, 1389 BS and it was agreed upon that the sale deed would be executed and registered within 2 months from the date of payment of money. It is alleged that Gouranga Chandra suddenly died but after agreement the suit even has not been filed within 3 years from the date of death of Gouranga Chandra: The suit has been filed admittedly on 21-16-90 corresponding to 5-7-1397 BS. So, the trial Court rightly held that the suit is barred by limitation. 

 12. But the appellate Court ignored this point of law altogether while decreeing the suit for specific performance of contract. It has been stated in the plaint and the specific case of the plaintiffs is that the sale was to be effected within two months from the date of agreement. In that view of the matter, the time limit has become essence of the contract in this suit. So, the suit having been filed long after, three years, it is highly barred by limitation. 

 18. Section 53 of the Specific Relief Act comes up to fix up the limitation of the specific performance of contract and time limit becomes the essence of the contract and the responsibility is cast upon the plaintiff in carrying out the contract in time. 

 20. The plaintiff's suit after 8 years of death of Gouranga Chandra, on the basis of an alleged oral agreement is definitely barred by limitation. Moreover, it is understood from the meticulous reading of the evidence on record and from the judgments of the courts below that the plaintiff could not prove even payment of the consideration money and delivery of possession.
